Enonce: As a Business administrator, I want to match OIDC claim values with a regular expression in a mapping entry, so that one rule covers all matching subgroups.
As a Business administrator, I want to choose Static or Regex per entry, so that existing exact-match mappings keep working unchanged.
Couverture: Couverte via FR-1, FR-3, FR-7, FR-8

Enonce: As a Business administrator, I want an invalid regex rejected when I save, so that a broken pattern never silently denies or over-grants access.
As an End user, I want my Roles and Teams resolved correctly from my group claims at login, so that a new subgroup gives the right access with no admin action.
A Business administrator can set each claim mapping entry's match type to Static or Regex; a new entry defaults to Static.
For a Regex entry, Horizon grants the entry's Roles and Teams when an extracted claim value matches the pattern over its whole length.
A Static entry keeps matching by exact string equality, unchanged.
When a claim value matches several entries, Horizon grants the union of all matched entries' Roles and Teams.
Regex matching is case-sensitive; case-insensitive matching is expressed with inline regex flags.
Horizon validates a Regex entry's pattern when the OIDC provider is saved and rejects the save with a clear error naming the offending entry.
A Regex entry references only existing Roles and Teams, validated at save time as today.
The extended claim mapping is included in configuration import / export.
Regex entry app-team-.* mapped to Team X; login with app-team-frontend and app-team-backend grants Team X.
Invalid pattern app-team-[ is rejected on save with an error naming the entry; mapping not persisted.
Static entry admin -> Role A and Regex entry admin.* -> Role B; login with admin grants both roles.
Regex entry team-.* mapped to Team Y; value x-team-frontend does not match, Team Y not granted.
Mapping saved before upgrade with exact-match entries: after upgrade every entry is Static and resolution is identical to 2.10.
Configuring the OIDC provider claim mapping, including regex entries, is permitted to the Business administrator using the existing Identity Provider management permission; no new permission.
Backward compatibility: stored mappings load unchanged, every existing entry is Static, no data migration beyond defaulting.
Regex evaluation must be safe against pathological input (ReDoS guard, approach still an open question).
Saving the provider emits the existing audit event SEC-IDENTITY-PROVIDER-UPDATE; no new event type.
Mapping is stored per tenant in the identity providers configuration; the Match type control is not expert-mode only.
Existing synchronization modes (roles_teams, roles, teams) keep their semantics with Regex entries (not in the spec, present in the code).
